result.question: Latest deep learning architectures for writer identification / writer retrieval in 2023-2025, especially those evaluated on the CVL Database: (1) current state-of-the-art including self-supervised Vision Transformers (DINO), ViT, and Transformer-based approaches; (2) comparison with earlier CNN-based architectures (ResNet, VGG) and classical methods (SIFT+Fisher Vector/VLAD); (3) benchmark results (Top-1 accuracy, mAP) on CVL Database; (4) accurate academic citations usable for a thesis, including architecture name, authors, venue/year, and CVL results where available.
result.summary: The question targets recent (2023-2025) deep-learning writer identification/retrieval methods benchmarked on the CVL Database, spanning cutting-edge self-supervised ViT/DINO/Transformer approaches, their lineage from CNN and classical SIFT+FV/VLAD baselines, reported CVL metrics, and citable academic references. I split it into angles covering the SOTA transformer methods, the CNN/classical baselines for comparison, CVL-specific benchmark numbers, the venue/citation trail, and the DINO self-supervised sub-thread specifically.

angles.rationale: A recent survey consolidates the field's taxonomy and dataset landscape, giving a citable overview and pointers to method papers.

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (Raven, Matei, Fink; TU Dortmund, 2024)
results.snippet: The most directly relevant recent SOTA paper. Trains a ViT self-supervised (DINO-style, no labels), extracts local foreground features and aggregates via VLAD. On CVL Database achieves 98.6% mAP and 99.4% Top-1 accuracy (with reranking), and sets new SOTA on Historical-WI (83.1% mAP) and HisIR19 (95.0% mAP). Full author, venue (arXiv Sept 2024), and CVL numbers for a thesis comparison table.

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (full HTML text)
results.snippet: Full-text HTML version containing the detailed CVL benchmark tables comparing the ViT+VLAD approach against prior CNN/ResNet and SIFT+Fisher Vector/VLAD baselines. Useful to extract exact per-method mAP and Top-1 numbers and citations for the results table.

results.title: Writer identification and writer retrieval based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli, IET Biometrics 2022)
results.snippet: Strong CNN-based baseline (ResNet + NetVLAD + reranking) that reports 98.4% mAP on CVL. Represents the pre-Transformer SOTA and is a key comparison point against the 2024 ViT results. Peer-reviewed venue, citable for thesis.

results.title: Writer Retrieval using Compact Convolutional Transformers and NetMVLAD (Peer et al.)
results.snippet: Bridges CNN and Transformer approaches using Compact Convolutional Transformers with a learned NetMVLAD aggregator, evaluated on CVL and Historical-WI. Important intermediate architecture for showing the CNN-to-Transformer transition in writer retrieval.

results.title: Evaluating learned feature aggregators for writer retrieval (2024)
results.snippet: Recent (2024) comparative study of learned aggregation methods (VLAD, NetVLAD, etc.) for writer retrieval including CVL evaluation. Useful for contextualizing the aggregation-stage choices and their effect on mAP/Top-1.

results.title: Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets (Fink group, 2023)
results.snippet: 2023 work from the same research line establishing the SIFT/CNN + VLAD pipeline and reranking baselines later compared against ViT. Provides methodology and baseline CVL/Historical-WI numbers, and accurate citations for the classical-to-deep progression.

results.title: Christlein et al. — Writer Identification Using GMM Supervectors and Exemplar-SVMs (Pattern Recognition 2017)
results.snippet: The canonical classical/handcrafted baseline for the comparative section: RootSIFT descriptors densely sampled at script contours, encoded with GMM supervectors and refined with Exemplar-SVMs. Evaluated on ICDAR13, CVL, and KHATT; compares GMM supervectors vs Fisher Vectors vs VLAD (on CVL, FV/VLAD outperform; on ICDAR13, GMM supervectors win). Christlein, Bernecker, Honig, Maier, Angelopoulou, Pattern Recognition 63:258-267, 2017 — the standard SIFT+FV/VLAD citation.

results.title: Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli — Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (IET Biometrics 2022)
results.snippet: Directly bridges CNN and classical baselines: ResNet-20 feature extractor with a learnable NetVLAD layer (a neural analog of VLAD/Fisher Kernel). Reports concrete CVL numbers — on CVL page level ResNet20+VLAD reaches 97.4% mAP / 99.2% Top-1 and ResNet20+NetVLAD 97.0% mAP / 98.9% Top-1, outperforming SIFT+VLAD. Excellent for the CNN-vs-classical encoding comparison with exact benchmark figures.

results.title: Christlein et al. — Unsupervised Feature Learning for Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval (ICDAR 2017)
results.snippet: Foundational self-supervised/CNN baseline predating the ViT era: trains a ResNet on SIFT-based surrogate cluster labels (SIFT patches, indices of SIFT descriptor clusters as targets), then encodes CNN activations with VLAD/GMM. Bridges handcrafted SIFT features and deep learning; strong CVL and ICDAR13 mAP results. Key prior-work citation showing the SIFT->CNN transition.

results.title: Fiel & Sablatnig — Offline Writer Identification Using CNN Activation Features (also 'Writer Identification and Retrieval Using a CNN')
results.snippet: One of the earliest CNN baselines for writer ID: uses activation features from a CNN (Caffe-style) as writer descriptors, aggregated and compared, evaluated on CVL and ICDAR datasets. Frequently cited as the first-generation deep-learning baseline that replaced handcrafted features and is the reference point for later ResNet/VGG comparisons.

results.title: Christlein & Maier — Encoding CNN Activations for Writer Recognition (DAS 2018)
results.snippet: Systematically compares encoding of deep CNN activations (VLAD, Fisher Vectors, GMM supervectors) for writer recognition, showing VLAD/multi-VLAD aggregation of ResNet activations on CVL/ICDAR13. Useful for justifying the choice of feature-encoding method when moving from CNN embeddings to a global writer descriptor.

results.title: WriterINet: a multi-path deep CNN for offline text-independent writer identification (IJDAR 2022)
results.snippet: Recent (2022) multi-path deep CNN baseline reporting state-of-the-art Top-1 on CVL and IAM among CNN methods, with the standard train/encode/compare pipeline. Serves as a modern CNN reference point to contrast against Transformer/DINO approaches in the comparative-analysis section.

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (Raven, Seuret et al., 2024, arXiv / accepted ICDAR-track work)
results.snippet: Directly answers the core question. Trains a ViT self-supervised (no labels), extracts local foreground features and aggregates with VLAD. Sets SOTA on CVL: 98.6% mAP and 99.4% Top-1 with reranking, no ViT fine-tuning. Also reports Historical-WI 83.1% mAP and HisIR19 95.0% mAP. Shows local features beat the ViT class token. The single most citable recent Transformer paper with concrete CVL numbers.

results.title: Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli, 2020/2022, IET Biometrics)
results.snippet: The strong CNN+NetVLAD baseline the ViT work is compared against. ResNet20 + NetVLAD (+ reranking) reaches ~99% Top-1 / high mAP on CVL, outperforming SIFT+VLAD and ResNet20+VLAD. Essential for the (2) CNN-vs-Transformer and (3) benchmark-comparison parts of the thesis, and documents the classical SIFT/VLAD-to-deep progression.

results.title: Decorrelation-based Self-Supervised Visual Representation Learning for Writer Identification (Chattopadhyay et al., 2024, arXiv)
results.snippet: Very recent (Oct 2024) self-supervised representation learning specifically for writer ID, complementary to the DINO/ViT line. Useful for the SSL angle of the survey and for contrasting decorrelation-based SSL with contrastive and ViT approaches; reports results on standard writer benchmarks.

results.title: End-To-End Evaluation of Deep Learning Architectures for Off-Line Handwriting Writer Identification: A Comparative Study (Suteddy et al., JOIV Int. J. on Informatics Visualization)
results.snippet: A comparative/benchmark-style study across deep architectures for offline writer identification — closest match to the requested survey/overview angle. Useful for consolidating the CNN-era landscape and evaluation methodology; note the venue is a smaller journal, so verify its exact CVL figures before citing.

results.title: Enhancing writer identification and writer retrieval with CenSurE and Vision Transformers (2024, Technology Audit and Production Reserves)
results.snippet: Recent (2024) Transformer-based writer ID/retrieval combining a CenSurE keypoint detector with ViT features. Relevant to the ViT/Transformer focus and keypoint+encoding pipeline discussion; lower-tier venue, so treat its numbers as supporting rather than primary evidence.

results.title: Towards the Influence of Text Quantity on Writer Retrieval (2025, arXiv)
results.snippet: 2025 study analyzing how the amount of handwritten text affects retrieval performance, comparing ResNet vs. Transformer feature extractors and VLAD-style encoding on standard benchmarks (incl. CVL). Useful for the benchmark/methodology section and for a current (2025) data point on encoding and feature-count saturation (ResNet saturates ~1k features/line vs. SIFT to ~5k).

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (Raven, Matei & Fink, arXiv 2024)
results.snippet: THE central paper for this angle. Uses a Vision Transformer trained self-supervised (DINO-style, no labels); foreground patch tokens are extracted as local features and encoded with VLAD. Reports state-of-the-art 98.6% mAP on CVL Database with NO fine-tuning of the ViT, plus new SOTA on Historical-WI (83.1% mAP) and HisIR19 (95.0% mAP), beating prior methods by 2.5% and 1.8% mAP. Directly answers SOTA + self-supervised ViT/DINO + CVL benchmark. Cite as Raven, Matei, Fink (2024).

results.title: SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval (arXiv 2024)
results.snippet: Self-supervised pretraining strategy for writer retrieval: applies Segment Anything (SAM) to extract handwriting, then trains a Vision Transformer as a masked autoencoder to reconstruct masked patches predicting HOG features. Key example of the SSL/masked-image-modeling sub-thread for writer retrieval and reports historical benchmark results; strong comparison point to the DINO-VLAD approach.

results.title: Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets (Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig, arXiv/ICDAR 2023)
results.snippet: Cross-dataset writer retrieval work that trains local descriptors in a self-supervised / unsupervised manner (SIFT keypoints + NetVLAD-style aggregation) and evaluates across modern and historical sets including CVL. Useful bridge between classic SIFT+VLAD/Fisher pipelines and the newer transformer methods; good for the 'comparison with prior methods' part of the thesis.

results.title: Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli, IET Biometrics 2022)
results.snippet: CNN baseline for the comparison axis: ResNet-20 feature extractor with an integrated NetVLAD layer plus re-ranking, achieving 98.4% mAP on CVL. Represents the ResNet+NetVLAD (deep VLAD) generation that the 2024 self-supervised ViT (98.6% mAP) is measured against — essential for the CNN-vs-Transformer benchmark table.

results.title: Offline Writer Identification Using Convolutional Neural Network Activation Features (arXiv 2024, journal reprint)
results.snippet: Documents the CNN-activation-feature lineage (encoding pretrained CNN activations, SIFT+CNN patches) with CVL results reported up to ~99.4% Top-1 accuracy. Good for tracing the CNN/ResNet + Fisher/VLAD baselines and their CVL Top-1 numbers that precede the transformer era.

results.title: Contrastive Masked Autoencoders for Character-Level Open-Set Writer Identification (2024/2025)
results.snippet: Combines contrastive learning with masked autoencoding for writer identification — squarely in the self-supervised/contrastive pretraining sub-thread requested. Character-level, open-set framing complements the document-level DINO-VLAD approach; useful to show breadth of SSL strategies (contrastive vs distillation vs MAE) in 2023-2025.

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (Raven, Matei & Fink, 2024)
results.snippet: The single most on-target paper. A self-supervised ViT (comparing DINO, iBOT, AttMask) whose local foreground token features are aggregated with VLAD. Reports CVL Database 98.6% mAP and 99.4% Top-1 (with reranking) WITHOUT fine-tuning, plus SOTA on Historical-WI (83.1% mAP) and HisIR19 (95.0% mAP). Explicitly frames the shift from handcrafted/CNN features to Transformers, and shows foreground tokens beat the ViT class token. Authors: Tim Raven, Arthur Matei, Gernot A. Fink; arXiv Sept 2024 (cs.CV).

results.title: SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval (Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig, ICDAR 2024)
results.snippet: 2024 Transformer/self-supervised approach from TU Wien CVL. Uses a ViT encoder-decoder that reconstructs HOG features of binarized (Segment-Anything-extracted) handwriting during pretraining, then fine-tunes with NetRVLAD as encoding layer. Historical-WI 73.3% mAP, HisFrag20 57.2% mAP (+11.6 pts over prior), GRK-Papyri 58.0% Top-1. Directly relevant for the self-supervised ViT angle, though evaluated on historical rather than CVL.

results.title: Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets (Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig, ICDAR 2023)
results.snippet: Introduces NetRVLAD, a lighter alternative to NetVLAD, trained on 32x32 SIFT-keypoint patches with a residual backbone, plus Similarity Graph Reranking. SOTA on ICDAR17 (80.6% mAP) and ICDAR19 (93.2% mAP). Key 2023 reference bridging classic SIFT/VLAD pipelines and modern deep aggregation; code on GitHub (marco-peer/icdar23). Springer/ACM ICDAR 2023 proceedings.

results.title: Writer Retrieval using Compact Convolutional Transformers and NetMVLAD (Peer et al., 2022)
results.snippet: Early Transformer-based writer retrieval WITH explicit CVL numbers: a CCT7 (Compact Convolutional Transformer) pretrained on CIFAR-100 with NetMVLAD achieves 96.5% mAP on CVL and 89.3% mAP on ICDAR2013. Useful as the Transformer baseline on CVL to contrast against the 2024 self-supervised ViT (98.6%).

results.title: Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli, 2020)
results.snippet: CNN + NetVLAD baseline with reranking, a widely cited pre-Transformer reference point on CVL/ICDAR. Good for the 'comparison with earlier CNN/VLAD methods' part of the thesis and to establish how much the ViT era improved Top-1/mAP.

results.title: Encoding CNN Activations for Writer Recognition (Christlein & Maier, 2017/2018)
results.snippet: Foundational CNN-era method: encodes deep activations (VLAD/Fisher-style) for writer identification, part of the SIFT+Fisher Vector to CNN lineage. Provides the classical/CNN baseline context that the Transformer SOTA is measured against on CVL and ICDAR benchmarks.

results.title: Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval (Raven, Matei, Fink — 2024, arXiv / ICDAR-track)
results.snippet: Current SOTA. Authors: Tim Raven, Arthur Matei, Gernot A. Fink (TU Dortmund). Uses a self-supervised (DINO-style) Vision Transformer as feature extractor; patch tokens with foreground extracted as local features and encoded with VLAD. Reports 98.6% mAP on CVL Database (no fine-tuning), plus Historical-WI 83.1% mAP and HisIR19 95.0% mAP. The single most citable recent DINO/ViT paper for the thesis, with direct CVL benchmark numbers and comparison against prior CNN methods.

results.title: Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Using Vision Transformer for Forensic Documents (DAS 2022, Springer LNCS)
results.snippet: Document Analysis Systems (DAS) 2022 paper introducing a plain ViT for writer ID/retrieval as an alternative to CNN SOTA. Reports up to 99% Top-1 accuracy on CVL and 97% on ICDAR 2013. Clean, well-defined venue citation (LNCS 13237) and provides ViT Top-1 numbers on CVL, useful as the transition point from CNN to Transformer approaches.

results.title: Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets (Peer, Kleber, Sablatnig — ICDAR 2023)
results.snippet: ICDAR 2023 (San José) paper from TU Wien CVL group applying self-supervised Vision Transformers to writer retrieval. Strong, correctly-attributable ICDAR citation from the group that maintains the CVL Database; establishes the self-supervised ViT + aggregation (VLAD) pipeline that the 2024/2025 SOTA builds on.

results.title: SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval (Peer et al. — ICDAR 2024)
results.snippet: ICDAR 2024 self-supervised pretraining strategy: Segment Anything (SAM) to extract handwriting, then a ViT masked-autoencoder reconstructing HOG features of masked patches. Represents the 2024 self-supervised ViT frontier and is evaluated on standard writer-retrieval benchmarks including CVL-family datasets — good for the SSL/ViT section of the thesis.

results.title: Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking (Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli — IET Biometrics, 2022)
results.snippet: Represents the CNN + NetVLAD + re-ranking lineage (the pre-Transformer SOTA baseline). Journal-quality citation (IET Biometrics) reporting CVL results; essential for the comparison section contrasting classic SIFT/Fisher-Vector and CNN-based aggregation against the newer ViT/DINO methods.

results.title: Interpretable Writer Recognition via Vectors of Locally Aggregated Characters (ICDAR 2025, Springer LNCS)
results.snippet: ICDAR 2025 proceedings paper (VLAC — Vectors of Locally Aggregated Characters). Recent 2025 architecture reporting new state-of-the-art retrieval results on CVL and evaluated on CVL, IAM and Historical-WI. Useful as the most up-to-date (2025) benchmark point and for the interpretability angle versus black-box ViT embeddings.

claims.claim: The paper 'Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval' by Tim Raven, Arthur Matei, and Gernot A. Fink (TU Dortmund University, arXiv:2409.00751, September 2024) uses a self-supervised ViT-small/16 trained with AttMask (an iBOT/DINO-based method) for writer retrieval.
claims.quote: We chose AttMask [20] for self-supervised training. The method is an adaptation of iBOT [37], which incorporates Masked Image Modeling (MIM) into the DINO [2] framework... Our model is a ViT-small/16 [12] with an input image size of 224.

claims.claim: On the CVL Database, the proposed self-supervised ViT method (VLAD-encoded foreground tokens with kRNN reranking) achieves 98.6% mAP and 99.4% Top-1 accuracy; without reranking it reaches 97.1% mAP and 99.4% Top-1.
claims.quote: VLAD-encoded foreground tokens with kRNN reranking: "98.6% mAP, 99.4% Top1" ... VLAD-encoded foreground tokens without reranking: "97.1% mAP, 99.4% Top1"

claims.claim: On CVL, the ViT-based method matches but does not clearly surpass prior CNN/handcrafted methods: Christlein et al. (VLAD + E-SVM reranking) achieves 98.4% mAP / 99.5% Top-1, and Rasoulzadeh (NetVLAD + kRNN) achieves 98.6% mAP / 99.2% Top-1.
claims.quote: Christlein et al. [10]: VLAD with E-SVM reranking - "98.4% mAP, 99.5% Top1" - Rasoulzadeh [31]: NetVLAD with kRNN reranking - "98.6% mAP, 99.2% Top1"

claims.claim: The authors frame their contribution as a departure from prior writer retrieval methods that rely on CNN activations or handcrafted local features.
claims.quote: Current writer retrieval and identification methods still rely on local features extracted from Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) activations [8] or handcrafted methods.

claims.claim: On the Historical-WI benchmark, the method outperforms a SIFT+Pathlet/VLAD baseline (Lai et al., 77.1% mAP) with 83.1% mAP using reranking, indicating stronger gains on historical data than on CVL.
claims.quote: Lai et al. (SIFT+Pathlet features with VLAD): 77.1% mAP - Their method: 83.1% mAP with reranking

claims.claim: A self-supervised Vision Transformer (trained without labels) with VLAD encoding of local foreground features achieves 98.6% mAP on the CVL Database without any fine-tuning, showing the ViT feature extractor transfers directly to modern datasets.
claims.quote: our ViT feature extractor can be directly applied to modern datasets such as the CVL database (98.6% mAP)

claims.claim: The same self-supervised ViT approach sets state-of-the-art on historical writer retrieval benchmarks, reaching 83.1% mAP on Historical-WI and 95.0% mAP on HisIR19 (HisIR19).
claims.quote: Historical-WI | 83.1% mAP (state-of-the-art)

claims.claim: For writer retrieval, extracting local foreground features from the ViT and aggregating them via VLAD outperforms using the ViT's class token.
claims.quote: extracting local foreground features is superior to using the ViT's class token

claims.claim: The model is trained self-supervised without labeled data, using a Vision Transformer instead of CNN-based or handcrafted-feature methods for writer retrieval.
claims.quote: the model is trained in a self-supervised fashion without any need for labels

claims.claim: Christlein et al. (2017) propose an offline writer identification method that uses RootSIFT descriptors computed densely at script contours, encoded via GMM supervectors, providing a strong classical (local-feature + statistical encoding) baseline that pre-dates CNN/Transformer approaches.
claims.quote: This paper describes a method for robust offline writer identification. We propose to use RootSIFT descriptors computed densely at the script contours. GMM supervectors are used as encoding method to describe the characteristic handwriting of an individual scribe.

claims.claim: The GMM-supervector + Exemplar-SVM method was evaluated on the CVL Database (among other benchmarks) and reported state-of-the-art results at the time, making it a canonical classical baseline to compare against modern deep-learning writer identification on CVL.
claims.quote: The authors evaluated their approach on three public datasets (ICDAR, CVL, KHATT) and achieved state-of-the-art results across all three benchmarks.

claims.claim: The paper was published in Pattern Recognition (Elsevier) in 2017 by V. Christlein, D. Bernecker, F. Hönig, A. Maier, and E. Angelopoulou, and is a highly-cited reference in writer identification (152 citations).
claims.quote: Authors: V Christlein, D Bernecker, F Hönig, A Maier, E Angelopoulou; Year: 2017; Venue: Pattern Recognition (Elsevier); Citation Count: 152 citations

claims.claim: CCT7 (Compact Convolutional Transformer) combined with NetMVLAD achieves 96.5% mAP on the CVL Database for writer retrieval.
claims.quote: CCT7 pretrained on CIFAR-100 combined with NetMVLAD achieves 89.3% Mean Average Precision (mAP) on the ICDAR2013 dataset and 96.5% on the CVL dataset.

claims.claim: The proposed Transformer-based approach (CCT) outperforms CNNs such as ResNet18 used in prior state-of-the-art writer retrieval while using only about one-third of the parameters.
claims.quote: CCTs outperform Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) used in current State-of-the-Art methods for writer retrieval, namely ResNet18, while at the same time only have one-third of the number of parameters.

claims.claim: The method learns patch embeddings at SIFT keypoint locations using a CCT followed by a NetMVLAD layer and Generalized Max Pooling to produce global page descriptors, bridging classic keypoint detection with Transformer encoding.
claims.quote: embeddings of patches extracted at SIFT keypoint locations are learned by a Compact Convolutional Transformer (CCT), a modified attention-based transformer architecture including convolutions, followed by a NetMVLAD layer and Generalized Max Pooling (GMP) to obtain global page descriptors

claims.claim: Net-MVLAD is proposed as an extension of NetVLAD using multiple vocabularies of different sizes to improve aggregation over the original NetVLAD.
claims.quote: Net-MVLAD is proposed as an extension of NetVLAD with multiple vocabularies, to encode information with different vocabulary sizes improving the original NetVLAD.

claims.claim: The paper was authored by Marco Peer, Florian Kleber, and Robert Sablatnig and published at ICPR 2022 (pages 1571-1578).
claims.quote: The work was authored by Marco Peer, Florian Kleber, and Robert Sablatnig, and published in ICPR 2022: 1571-1578.

claims.claim: The paper (Mattick, Mayr, Seuret, Kordon, Wu, Christlein) evaluates Transformers as learned feature aggregators for patch-based writer retrieval, comparing them against NetVLAD, and finds Transformers do not clearly outperform — 'the performance of transformers in this task has room for improvement.'
claims.quote: the performance of transformers in this task has room for improvement, highlighting the need for further research to enhance their effectiveness

claims.claim: The pipeline extracts patches, processes each patch independently with a ResNet-18 backbone, then aggregates all patch features into a single global descriptor via either a Transformer or a NetVLAD module, trained end-to-end.
claims.quote: patches are processed independently via a ResNet-18 model, and finally aggregates all patches via either a Transformer or NetVLAD model into a single global prediction, with the entire method trained end-to-end

claims.claim: The methods are evaluated on the CVL and IAM writer datasets.
claims.quote: The experiments were conducted on the CVL and IAM datasets

claims.claim: The paper is a peer-reviewed journal article: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition (IJDAR), Volume 27, Issue 3, pages 265-274, 2024.
claims.quote: International Journal on Document Analysis and Recognition, Volume 27, Issue 3 ... Year: 2024

claims.claim: The method is CNN-based, not Transformer/ViT: a ResNet backbone extracts features from 32x32 patches at SIFT keypoints, encoded by a proposed NetRVLAD layer plus SGR graph reranking.
claims.quote: Descriptors Cluster labels Keypoints 32×32 patches Documents NetRVLAD ResNet SIFT SGR Fig. 1: Overview of our proposed pipeline.

claims.claim: The approach is self-supervised/unsupervised, trained on pseudo-cluster labels obtained by clustering SIFT descriptors rather than writer labels.
claims.quote: This paper presents an unsupervised approach for writer retrieval based on clustering SIFT descriptors detected at keypoint locations resulting in pseudo-cluster labels.

claims.claim: On the modern ICDAR2013 dataset the method achieves 86.1% mAP and 98.5% Top-1 accuracy, beating a supervised NetVLAD approach on Top-1 but trailing Zernike+mVLAD (88.0/99.4) and supervised NetVLAD+kRNN-QE (97.4 mAP) on mAP.
claims.quote: our approach achieves a notable performance (86.1% mAP), in particular Top-1 accuracy (98.5%) ... Zernike+mVLAD [3] 88.0 99.4 NetRVLAD+kRNN-QE (supervised) [22] 97.4 97.4 NetRVLAD+SGRk=1 (ours) 86.1 98.5

claims.claim: The paper evaluates on Historical-WI, HisIR19 and ICDAR2013 but does NOT report results on the CVL Database; on HisIR19 it sets a new SOTA of 80.6% mAP and 91.1% Top-1.
claims.quote: our approach sets a new State-of-the-art performance with a mAP of 80.6% and a Top-1 accuracy of 91.1%.

claims.claim: Authors are Marco Peer, Florian Kleber and Robert Sablatnig of the Computer Vision Lab, TU Wien; published at ICDAR 2023 (arXiv:2305.05358, May 2023).
claims.quote: Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets Marco Peer, Florian Kleber, and Robert Sablatnig Computer Vision Lab TU Wien

claims.claim: The proposed method is a CNN-based pipeline using a ResNet-20 backbone with an integrated NetVLAD layer (inspired by VLAD), trained with a triplet semi-hard loss to learn embeddings of handwriting image patches.
claims.quote: Our proposed pipeline uses a ResNet-20 convolutional neural network with the NetVLAD layer, inspired by Vectors of Locally Aggregated Descriptors

claims.claim: The pipeline aggregates patch embeddings with generalized max-pooling and introduces a re-ranking strategy based on k-reciprocal nearest neighbors for identification and retrieval.
claims.quote: generalised max-pooling is employed for the aggregation of embedded descriptors of each handwritten image. A novel re-ranking strategy is introduced for the task of identification and retrieval based on k-reciprocal nearest neighbors

claims.claim: On the CVL Database the method achieves 98.4% mAP for writer retrieval (and 96.5% mAP on ICDAR 2013), reported as superior to prior methods in terms of mAP.
claims.quote: the results on the publicly available ICDAR13 and CVL datasets achieved 96.5% and 98.4% mAP, respectively

result.evidence: Primary source arXiv:2404.17221 confirms every element. It is titled/described as a self-supervised writer retrieval method. It uses a ViT masked autoencoder; the variant is ViT-4/8 meaning "patch size of four" and encoder "depth of 8" (decoder depth 1). It explicitly states it "propose[s] to reconstruct the HOG features of the binarized image" rather than raw pixels, because "by relying on binarization, the network automatically learns to focus on handwriting" and can "suppress the influence of the background." The masking (75% of tokens) and 32x32 color input token embedding are also described. The supporting quote matches the paper. No contradicting evidence found; claim is current (2024) and drawn from the primary source, matching claim strength.

Primary source arXiv:2404.17221 confirms all claim components. It states SAGHOG is "a self-supervised approach for writer retrieval" using a Vision Transformer masked autoencoder. ViT-4/8 is confirmed as a vanilla ViT with "patch size of four" and "depth of 8" encoder layers. Reconstruction target is confirmed: "Rather than reconstructing raw pixels like standard MAE, SAGHOG reconstructs HOG features" specifically "HOG features of the binarized image," so "the network automatically learns to focus on handwriting" and "suppress the influence of the background." Every element of the claim (self-supervised, ViT MAE, ViT-4/8, HOG-of-binarized-patches vs raw pixels) is directly and accurately supported. Source is the primary paper, current (2024), not marketing.

Primary source arXiv:2404.17221 (SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval, Peer/Kleber/Sablatnig, ICDAR2024) confirms evaluation only on three historical datasets: Historical-WI (3600 images, 760 writers), HisFrag20 (20019 test fragments, 1152 writers), and GRK-Papyri (50 docs, 10 writers). CVL Database is not used for evaluation and is not mentioned anywhere in the paper or abstract. Pretraining used CLaMM 2016/2017, Historical-WI train, cBAD 2019, HisIR19 — not CVL. The claim matches the quote and source exactly; no contradicting evidence found.

Primary source (arxiv.org/html/2404.17221, "SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval," Peer/Kleber/Sablatnig, ICDAR 2024) confirms evaluation on exactly three datasets: Historical-WI (3600 images, 760 writers), HisFrag20 (20019 test fragments, 1152 writers), and GRK-Papyri (50 docs, 10 writers). CVL Database is used neither for evaluation nor pretraining (pretraining used CLaMM, HisIR19, cBAD). Independent WebSearch corroborates: reported results are HisFrag20 mAP 57.2% and GRK-Papyri Top-1 58.0%, with no CVL benchmark. Claim is fully supported and current (2024 paper).

Every component of the claim is verbatim-supported by the primary source (arXiv 2404.17221, the SAGHOG paper). (1) Self-supervised writer retrieval: "self-supervised pretraining approach... training a vision transformer on reconstructing masked patches of the handwriting," finetuned by appending NetRVLAD for retrieval. (2) ViT masked autoencoder: "Saghog is based on the MAE architecture consisting of an encoder-decoder structure." (3) ViT-4/8: "We use the vanilla ViT structure with a patch size of four... We denote the encoder as ViT-4/8" (patch size 4, encoder depth 8). (4) HOG reconstruction of binarized patches instead of raw pixels: "we propose to reconstruct the HOG features of the binarized image due to two reasons. By relying on binarization, the network automatically learns to focus on handwriting." Source is the primary paper, current (2024), not marketing. No contradicting evidence found. Minor note: SAGHOG's headline evaluation is on historical datasets (HisFrag20, mAP 57.2%), not primarily CVL, but the claim itself makes no CVL assertion, so this does not affect correctness of the claim.

The primary source (SAGHOG paper, arXiv:2404.17221, "SAGHOG: Self-Supervised Autoencoder for Generating HOG Features for Writer Retrieval") was fetched directly. Its experimental evaluation (Section 4.1) benchmarks exactly three datasets: Historical-WI (3600 images, 760 writers), HisFrag20 (20019 test fragments, 1152 writers), and GRK-Papyri (50 documents, 10 writers). CVL Database is not mentioned anywhere in the paper. (CLaMM 2016/2017, cBAD 2019, HisIR19 appear only as self-supervised pretraining data, not CVL.) result.summary: Untuk writer identification/retrieval yang dievaluasi pada CVL Database, lanskap 2023-2025 menunjukkan bahwa pendekatan berbasis Transformer/self-supervised ViT sudah mulai menyamai—tetapi belum secara jelas melampaui—metode CNN dan klasik yang sudah matang. State-of-the-art terbaru yang paling relevan adalah "Self-Supervised Vision Transformers for Writer Retrieval" (Raven, Matei & Fink, TU Dortmund, ICDAR 2024, arXiv:2409.00751), sebuah ViT-small/16 yang dilatih dengan AttMask (berbasis iBOT/DINO) dan meng-encode token foreground lokal dengan VLAD, mencapai 98.6% mAP dan 99.4% Top-1 pada CVL (dengan kRNN reranking) tanpa fine-tuning. Angka ini praktis setara dengan metode CNN/klasik yang lebih lama: Christlein et al. (VLAD + Exemplar-SVM) 98.4% mAP / 99.5% Top-1, Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli (ResNet-20 + NetVLAD + kRNN) 98.6% mAP / 99.2% Top-1, dan Christlein et al. GCPR 2015 (fitur aktivasi CNN + GMM supervector) 99.4% Top-1 / 97.8% mAP—yang menunjukkan CVL adalah benchmark yang sudah "jenuh" di sekitar 99% Top-1. Penting untuk thesis: dua metode Transformer/self-supervised paling baru yang berbasis ViT-MAE (SAGHOG, ICDAR 2024) dan pipeline NetRVLAD+SGR (Peer et al., ICDAR 2023) sebenarnya TIDAK dievaluasi pada CVL—keduanya fokus pada dataset historis—sehingga satu-satunya arsitektur ViT/DINO 2023-2025 dengan angka CVL yang bisa disitasi adalah Raven et al. 2024. Metode CNN (WriterINet dual-stream ResNet-50+DenseNet-201, IJDAR 2023) dan berbasis Convolutional Transformer (CCT7+NetMVLAD, ICPR 2022, 96.5% mAP) melengkapi peta perbandingan.

findings.claim: SOTA ViT/self-supervised terbaru pada CVL: Raven, Matei & Fink (TU Dortmund, ICDAR 2024, arXiv:2409.00751) memakai ViT-small/16 yang dilatih self-supervised dengan AttMask (adaptasi iBOT yang menanamkan Masked Image Modeling ke framework DINO), meng-encode token foreground lokal dengan VLAD dan reranking kRNN. Mencapai 98.6% mAP / 99.4% Top-1 pada CVL (dengan reranking) dan 97.1% mAP / 99.4% Top-1 tanpa reranking, tanpa fine-tuning.
findings.evidence: Sumber primer arXiv:2409.00751v1 mengonfirmasi verbatim: model 'ViT-small/16 with an input image size of 224', pelatihan 'AttMask ... an adaptation of iBOT ... which incorporates Masked Image Modeling (MIM) into the DINO framework', dan Tabel CVL: VLAD-encoded foreground tokens tanpa reranking = 97.1% mAP/99.4% Top-1, dengan kRNN reranking = 98.6% mAP/99.4% Top-1. Abstrak menyatakan 'ViT feature extractor can be directly applied to modern datasets such as the CVL database (98.6% mAP) without any fine-tuning'. Ini satu-satunya arsitektur ViT/DINO 2023-2025 dengan angka CVL eksplisit.

findings.claim: Pada CVL, metode ViT self-supervised (Raven et al. 2024) menyamai tetapi tidak jelas melampaui metode CNN/handcrafted sebelumnya. Perbandingan langsung di paper: Christlein et al. (VLAD + E-SVM reranking) = 98.4% mAP / 99.5% Top-1; Rasoulzadeh (NetVLAD + kRNN) = 98.6% mAP / 99.2% Top-1; metode ViT = 98.6% mAP / 99.4% Top-1. CVL adalah benchmark jenuh di sekitar 99% Top-1.

findings.claim: SAGHOG (Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig, TU Wien, ICDAR 2024, arXiv:2404.17221) adalah metode writer retrieval self-supervised berbasis Vision Transformer masked autoencoder (ViT-4/8) yang merekonstruksi fitur HOG dari patch tulisan tangan yang di-binarisasi (bukan piksel mentah). PENTING: TIDAK dievaluasi pada CVL Database—hanya pada dataset historis (Historical-WI, HisFrag20, GRK-Papyri).
findings.evidence: Sumber primer mengonfirmasi ViT masked autoencoder yang merekonstruksi 'HOG features of the binarized image' dengan masking 75% token; ViT-4/8 = patch size 4, encoder depth 8. Evaluasi eksklusif pada Historical-WI (760 penulis), HisFrag20 (1152 penulis), GRK-Papyri (10 penulis). CVL tidak disebut. Untuk thesis: dapat disitasi sebagai arsitektur ViT-MAE terbaru namun tanpa angka CVL.

findings.claim: Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig (TU Wien, ICDAR 2023, arXiv:2305.05358) 'Towards Writer Retrieval for Historical Datasets' mengusulkan pipeline unsupervised berbasis CNN (BUKAN ViT): SIFT keypoints + backbone ResNet (embedding 64-dim) + lapisan NetRVLAD (modifikasi NetVLAD tanpa normalisasi) + Similarity Graph Reranking (SGR). TIDAK dievaluasi pada CVL—hanya Historical-WI, HisIR19, ICDAR2013.
findings.evidence: Sumber primer mengonfirmasi ResNet (default ResNet56) menghasilkan embedding 64-dim, NetRVLAD menghilangkan lapisan normalisasi/inisialisasi, dan SGR sebagai langkah reranking berbasis graph. Evaluasi hanya pada tiga dataset; CVL hanya muncul di Related Work, bukan sebagai dataset evaluasi.

findings.claim: Baseline CNN kuat pada CVL: Rasoulzadeh & BabaAli 'Writer Identification and Writer Retrieval Based on NetVLAD with Re-ranking' (IET Biometrics 2022, DOI 10.1049/bme2.12039; arXiv:2012.06186). Pipeline CNN: ResNet-20 + lapisan NetVLAD terintegrasi, dilatih triplet semi-hard loss, agregasi generalized max-pooling, PCA, dan reranking k-reciprocal nearest neighbor + query expansion (krNN-QE). Pada CVL: 98.6% mAP / 99.2% Top-1 (k=2), menetapkan SOTA baru pada Hard-3 dan mAP namun sedikit di bawah Christlein pada Top-1/Hard-2.
findings.evidence: Sumber primer (jurnal + preprint) mengonfirmasi semua komponen pipeline verbatim. Tabel 2 CVL-283: proposed ResNet-20+NetVLAD+krNN-QE k=2 = Top-1 99.2/Hard-2 98.9/Hard-3 98.0/mAP 98.6; Christlein ResNet-20+VLAD+ESVM = Top-1 99.5/Hard-2 99.0/Hard-3 97.7/mAP 98.4. Catatan: paper 2021/2022, di luar jendela 2023-2025 tapi merupakan baseline CNN kanonik.

findings.claim: Baseline klasik kanonik pada CVL: Christlein, Bernecker, Hönig, Maier & Angelopoulou 'Writer Identification Using GMM Supervectors and Exemplar-SVMs' (Pattern Recognition 63:258-267, 2017, PII S0031320316303211). Metode klasik (tanpa deep learning): RootSIFT dense pada kontur skrip + encoding GMM supervector + Exemplar-SVM. Dievaluasi pada ICDAR, CVL, KHATT dengan hasil SOTA (~99% Top-1 pada CVL).

findings.claim: Baseline CNN awal pada CVL: Christlein, Bernecker, Maier & Angelopoulou 'Offline Writer Identification Using Convolutional Neural Network Activation Features' (GCPR 2015, LNCS 9358 pp. 540-552, DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-24947-6_45; arXiv:2402.17029). Fitur aktivasi CNN dari patch 32x32 + encoding GMM supervector dengan normalisasi KL-Kernel (adaptasi hanya mean). Pada CVL: Top-1 = 0.994, mAP = 0.978 (Hard Top-2 0.988, Top-3 0.973, Top-4 0.926). findings.claim: WriterINet (IJDAR 26, 2023, DOI 10.1007/s10032-022-00418-3) adalah arsitektur CNN dua-stream (multi-path): fine-tuning ResNet-50 + DenseNet-201—BUKAN Transformer/ViT. Dievaluasi pada banyak benchmark termasuk CVL, dengan performa tertinggi atau kompetitif vs SOTA.
findings.evidence: Abstrak paper (peer-reviewed Springer/IJDAR 2023) mengonfirmasi 'two CNN streams derived from fine-tuning the ResNet-50 and DenseNet-201 models' dan evaluasi pada IAM, ICDAR2013, CVL, IFN/ENIT, ICDAR2011, Firemaker, CERUG dengan performa tertinggi/kompetitif. Angka Top-1/mAP CVL spesifik tidak dapat diekstrak (paywall).

findings.claim: CCT7 (Compact Convolutional Transformer) + NetMVLAD (Peer, Kleber & Sablatnig, ICPR 2022) mencapai 96.5% mAP pada CVL untuk writer retrieval (89.3% pada ICDAR2013). Merupakan pendekatan Convolutional Transformer, tapi bukan SOTA pada CVL.
findings.evidence: Abstrak (dikonfirmasi via repositori TU Wien repositum.tuwien.at) menyatakan 'CCT7 pretrained on CIFAR-100 combined with NetMVLAD achieves 89.3% mAP on ICDAR2013 and 96.5% on CVL'. 96.5% di bawah metode VLAD+E-SVM (98.4%) dan ViT self-supervised (98.6%). Paper 2022, sedikit di luar jendela 2023-2025.

result.caveats: 1) Jendela waktu: Dari semua arsitektur ViT/Transformer/DINO 2023-2025 yang ditemukan, hanya SATU (Raven, Matei & Fink, ICDAR 2024, arXiv:2409.00751) yang benar-benar melaporkan angka pada CVL Database (98.6% mAP / 99.4% Top-1). Dua metode Transformer/self-supervised terbaru lainnya (SAGHOG ICDAR 2024; Peer et al. NetRVLAD+SGR ICDAR 2023) TIDAK dievaluasi pada CVL—keduanya fokus pada dataset historis. Beberapa baseline kuat (Rasoulzadeh 2021/2022, CCT7 2022, WriterINet 2023) berada di atau sedikit di luar jendela 2023-2025. 2) Saturasi benchmark: CVL adalah dataset yang sudah jenuh—banyak metode (klasik, CNN, ViT) mencapai ~99% Top-1 dan ~98% mAP, sehingga perbedaan antar-arsitektur sangat kecil dan mAP lebih diskriminatif daripada Top-1. Klaim 'SOTA' pada CVL harus dinyatakan hati-hati. 3) Akurasi sitasi: DOI 10.1007/978-3-319-24947-6_45 adalah paper Christlein et al. GCPR 2015 (CNN activation features), BUKAN Fiel & Sablatnig CAIP—kesalahan sitasi umum yang harus dihindari di thesis. 4) Angka spesifik yang ditolak: Klaim tentang angka presisi CVL dari Christlein & Maier DAS 2018 (Top-1 99.6/mAP 98.0 untuk VLAD+E-SVM) DITOLAK verifikasi; jangan sitasi angka presisi tersebut—gunakan hanya deskripsi metodologi. 5) Kualitas sumber: Angka Top-1/mAP CVL WriterINet tidak dapat diverifikasi (Springer paywall); CCT7 diverifikasi via repositori institusi karena akses IEEE terbatas.
openQuestions: Apakah ada arsitektur DINO/ViT self-supervised murni (bukan AttMask/iBOT, misalnya DINOv2) yang dievaluasi pada CVL Database dalam periode 2024-2025 yang belum tertangkap riset ini?
Berapa angka Top-1/mAP CVL yang tepat untuk WriterINet (ResNet-50+DenseNet-201) karena hanya klaim 'tertinggi atau kompetitif' yang bisa diverifikasi tanpa akses full-text?

Mengapa metode ViT/Transformer terbaru (SAGHOG, NetRVLAD+SGR) memilih tidak mengevaluasi pada CVL—apakah karena CVL dianggap terlalu jenuh/mudah sehingga fokus bergeser ke dataset historis yang lebih menantang?
Apakah keunggulan self-supervised ViT akan lebih jelas terlihat pada metrik atau kondisi lain (misalnya data terbatas, cross-dataset generalization) dibandingkan Top-1/mAP pada CVL yang sudah jenuh?
